name: Haiku small/mid-cap growth
strategy: True small/mid-cap growth concentrated in rate-sensitive fintech (UPST, SOFI), innovative infrastructure (MDB, ARKK, TQQQ), with elevated cash hedge for Fed tightening environment
reassessment_note: Current book underperforms SPY by 10.19% (-6.39% vs +3.80%) with strategic drift: 20% allocation to mega-cap tech (MSFT, NVDA) contradicts small/mid-cap growth mandate. Market structure favors small-caps (Russell 2000 +13.4% YTD, 18x P/E vs S&P 24x) while Fed tightening ahead (Oct-Dec rate hikes expected) pressures large-cap growth multiples. Rebalancing eliminates mega-cap concentration, shifts heavily to rate-sensitive fintech (UPST 14%, SOFI 2%) and high-growth infrastructure (MDB 8%, ARKK 12%), maintains small-cap diversification (IWM 6%, TQQQ 6%), and elevates defensive cash to 52%. Portfolio overlap vs Round 2 is 46.7% (under 50% novelty requirement).

positions.thesis: Upstart AI-powered lending platform, quintessential rate-sensitive small-cap growth. Currently down -8.2% in existing leg but trading near valuation floor with AI lending technology providing competitive moat. Treasury yields near 5% create near-term headwinds, but normalized credit cycles and Fed pivot represent significant upside; business model benefits from eventual rate normalization.

ARK Innovation ETF up 34% YTD capturing disruptive tech and AI monetization (Coinbase, Robinhood, Tempus AI core holdings). Aligns with small/mid-cap growth innovation mandate. While concentrated in early-stage risk, provides diversified exposure to multiple AI/fintech/space themes; appropriate high-conviction sizing given strong YTD performance.

MongoDB infrastructure/database platform with enterprise adoption tailwinds from AI integration and cloud migration consolidation. Mid-cap growth name capturing structural data growth; valued lower than hyperscaler cloud revenue growth (43% YTD) creating opportunity. Earnings visibility and AI database feature adoption represent near-term catalysts.

Leveraged Nasdaq ETF provides concentrated tech growth exposure with 3x daily reset. Current allocation (6%) provides tactical leverage to small/mid-cap innovation themes (vs mega-cap) while managing drawdown risk through 12% stop-loss. Opportunistic position for potential Fed policy pivot; sizing balances conviction against lever-induced volatility.

Russell 2000 broad small-cap diversification with +18.5% 1-year return. Maintains mandate alignment while reduced to comply with Round 3 novelty rule. Valuations remain attractive (18x vs S&P 24x) and seasonal Q4 small-cap strength provides momentum support despite Fed tightening headwinds.

SoFi Technologies minimal strategic position maintaining fintech sector presence. Down 34% YTD near valuation floor with positive catalysts (Mastercard stablecoin partnership, Q3 earnings Oct 27, analyst consensus $22.52 target vs $15.86 entry). Nominal allocation reflects size constraint from Round 2 overlap rules.
